title: The 5 Longest Years in the Solar System, Ranked (#1 Had One Birthday Since 1846)

scenes.text: Five planets, five very long years. Number one has barely had a birthday since 1846.

scenes.label: Mars · 687 days
scenes.text: Number five: Mars. A Martian year is six hundred eighty-seven Earth days, almost twice ours.

scenes.label: Jupiter · 12 years
scenes.text: Number four: Jupiter. One lap around the Sun takes almost twelve Earth years.

scenes.label: Saturn · 29 years
scenes.text: Number three: Saturn. Twenty-nine and a half years for a single trip around the Sun.

scenes.label: Uranus · 84 years
scenes.text: Number two: Uranus. Eighty-four years, about one human lifetime, for one orbit.

scenes.label: Neptune · 165 years
scenes.text: Number one: Neptune. About one hundred sixty-five years. It was found in 1846 and finished its first lap in 2011.

description:
The five longest years in the solar system, ranked by orbital period.
Neptune takes about 165 Earth years to circle the Sun, so it only completed its first full orbit since discovery in 2011.
Which planet's year would you most like to live through?
tags: how long is a year on neptune
first_comment: How old would you be on Neptune? And what should we rank next?
